Rashi on Pesachim 71b:10:1.hebrew: אימורי ציבור - קרבנות האמורין בציבור בשבת, כגון תמידין ומוספין, יוכיחו, שמותרין לשוחטן לשמן, והשוחט שאר זבחים לשמן בשבת חייב:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:10:1.english: Communal offerings - The offerings prescribed for the congregation on Shabbat, such as the daily offerings and additional offerings, prove [the matter], for they are permitted to be slaughtered for their own sake, yet one who slaughters other sacrifices for their sake on Shabbat is liable.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:10:2.hebrew: שיש להן קצבה - שאינו רואה אחרים הרבה עסוקין בשחיטתן, וכיון שנשחט התמיד, יודע הוא שאין צריך לשחוט עוד. הלכך, אין זה טועה אלא שוגג, דלא היה לו לטעות בדבר:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:10:2.english: Because they have a fixed limit - For he does not see many others occupied with slaughtering them, and once the daily offering has been slaughtered, he knows that there is no need to slaughter any more. Therefore, this [person] is not [considered] mistaken, rather an unwitting [transgressor], for he should not have erred in the matter.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:10:3.hebrew: תאמר בפסח שאין לו קצבה - שהכל צריכין לכך, והרי הוא רואה את אחרים הרבה עוסקין בכך וטרוד להתעסק במצוה, ואפילו שחט הוא פסחו כבר ומצא זבח זה עומד בעזרה, וכסבור שהוא פסח ושחטו לשם מי שהוא וטעה על כך. הלכך, טועה בדבר מצוה הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:10:3.english: Can you say [the same] about the Paschal lamb, which does not have a limit - For everyone needs [to offer] it, and behold, he sees many others engaged in it and is preoccupied with engaging in the mitzvah; and even if he himself has already slaughtered his Paschal lamb, and found this sacrifice standing in the [Temple] Courtyard, and thought that it was a Paschal lamb, and slaughtered it for the sake of someone [or other], and erred thereby. Therefore, he is [considered] one who erred in [the performance of] a mitzvah.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:11:1.hebrew: ר' מאיר אומר - השוחט אחרים כל שבתות שנה לשם אימורי ציבור, פטור:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:11:1.english: Rabbi Meir says - One who slaughters other [offerings] on all Sabbaths of the year for the sake of communal offerings is exempt.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:12:1.hebrew: שחטו בשבת שלא לאוכליו - דפסח פסול הוא, ונעלמה ממנו שבת או כסבור שכשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:12:1.english: [If] he slaughtered it on Shabbat for those who cannot eat it - For it is an invalid Paschal offering, and [either] Shabbat escaped his mind or he thought that it was valid.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:12:2.hebrew: שלא לאוכליו - לחולה ולזקן, חייב חטאת, דלא ניתנה לידחות שבת אצל שחיטה זו:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:12:2.english: For those who cannot eat it - [for example,] for a sick person or an elderly person, he is liable [to bring] a sin-offering, because Shabbat was not permitted to be overridden for this slaughter.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:12:3.hebrew: לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו וכו' פטור - דהא פסח כשר הוא, כדתנן בתמיד נשחט (ד' סא.), דמקצת אוכלין לא פסלי:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:12:3.english: For those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it, etc., he is exempt - For it is a valid Paschal offering, as we learned in [the chapter] Tamid Nishchat (61a), that [having] partial [fit] eaters does not disqualify [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:13:1.hebrew: שחטו ונמצא בעל מום חייב - דשוגג הוא ולא אנוס, דהוה ליה לבקוריה:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:13:1.english: [If] he slaughtered it and it was found [to have] a blemish, [he is] liable - For he is an unwitting transgressor and not [acting under] unavoidable circumstances, since he should have examined it.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:14:1.english: That the owners had withdrawn their hands - From it before slaughter, and registered for another [Paschal lamb].

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:14:2.hebrew: או שמתו או שנטמאו - דעכשיו לא ניתנה לידחות שבת אצלו:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:14:2.english: Or [that] they died or became ritually impure - for now Shabbat was not permitted to be overridden in his case.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:14:3.hebrew: פטור - שאנוס הוא, דלא היה יודע שכן, ולא היה לו לבדוק על כך:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:14:3.english: He is exempt - For he is [acting under] unavoidable circumstances, as he did not know that [it was] so, and he did not have to investigate this.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:1:1.hebrew: או אינו אלא ליום ולילה - דהאי בקר בוקרו של ט"ו קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:1:1.english: Or is it only for a day and a night - [Meaning] that this [word] "morning" refers to the morning of the fifteenth [of Nisan].

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:1:2.hebrew: כשהוא אומר ביום הראשון (לבקר) - מכלל דנאכלת כל יום הראשון של יום טוב, וקאמר לבקר דלא תלין עד בקר שני:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:1:2.english: When it says, "on the first day (until the morning)" - [This implies] by inference that it is eaten the entire first day of the Festival, and it says "until the morning" [meaning] that it shall not remain overnight until the second morning.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:2:1.hebrew: או אינו אלא בקר ראשון - לקמיה פריך: היכי תיסק אדעתין למימר תו? הא אמרת "ביום הראשון" חד, ו"לבקר" תרי:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:2:1.english: Or [perhaps] it is [eaten] only [until] the first morning - Later on, [the Gemara] asks: How could it enter our mind to say [this] anymore, [when] behold, you [already] said "on the first day" [indicates] one [day] and "until the morning" [indicates] two [days]?

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:2:2.hebrew: ומה אני מקיים חגיגה הנאכלת לשני ימים - דנפקא לן מקרא אחרינא דיש חגיגה נאכלת לשני ימים, ולקמן מפרש היכא אשכחן. ובאיזו חגיגה אני מקיימה? בשאר חגיגות חוץ מזו:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:2:2.english: And how do I establish a Festival peace-offering that is eaten for two days - For we derive from another verse that there is a Festival peace-offering eaten for two days, and later [the Gemara] explains where we find [it]. And regarding which Festival peace-offering do I establish it? [Regarding] other Festival peace-offerings, other than this one.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:2:3.hebrew: לימד על חגיגת י"ד כו' - ולקמן מפרש במאי מישתמע ליה, והשתא מפרש לה למתניתא, והדר אסיק אתקפתי' ד"תנא לבשר לא בעי ראשית":
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:2:3.english: It teaches regarding the Festival peace-offering of the fourteenth, etc. - And later [the Gemara] explains from what [phrase] it is implied to him, and now it explains the baraita, and afterward it concludes the objection [that] "the Tanna does not require reishit [first] for meat."

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:3:1.hebrew: כשהוא אומר אם נדר - באכילת שלמים שני ימים כתיב: "אם נדר או נדבה זבח קרבנו ביום הקריבו את זבחו יאכל וממחרת וגו'", הרי שני ימים ולילה שבינתיים. והוה ליה למיכתב "נדר ונדבה", "אם נדר" למה לי? ריבה אף שלמי חובה לאכילת שני ימים:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:3:1.english: When it says "If a vow" - Regarding the eating of peace-offerings [for] two days, [it is written:] "If the sacrifice of his offering is a vow or a freewill offering, on the day that he offers his sacrifice it shall be eaten, and on the morrow, etc." — behold, [this is] two days and the intervening night. Now, it should have written "a vow and a freewill offering"; why do I need "if a vow"? It [thereby] included even obligatory peace-offerings for eating [over] two days.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:3:2.hebrew: הכי קאמר או אינו - אלא ליום ולילה, והאי דכתב "ביום הראשון לבוקר" מילתא אחריתי היא, ובשתי חגיגות דיבר הכתוב: חגיגת ארבעה עשר וחמשה עשר, זו לבוקרה וזו לבוקרה. והכי משמע קרא: "לא ילין מבשר" חגיגת י"ד "אשר תזבח בערב", וסתם לינה לבוקרה משמע; ומאותה שתזבח "ביום הראשון", דהיינו חגיגת חמשה עשר, לא ילין לבוקר של ששה עשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:3:2.english: This is what [it] is saying: Or is it not - rather, [only] for a day and a night; and that which is written, "on the first day until the morning," is a separate matter, for the verse spoke of two Festival peace-offerings: the Festival peace-offering of the fourteenth and [that of] the fifteenth — this one until its morning, and this one until its morning. And this is what the verse means: "There shall not remain overnight any of the flesh" of the Festival peace-offering of the fourteenth "which you sacrifice in the evening," and an unspecified [prohibition of] remaining overnight implies until its [own] morning; and from that which you sacrifice "on the first day," which is the Festival peace-offering of the fifteenth, it shall not remain overnight until the morning of the sixteenth.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:4:1.hebrew: הדר אמר - תנא: "ומה אני מקיים חגיגה הנאכלת לשני ימים חוץ מזו?" כלומר: באיזו חגיגה חוץ מזו אני מקיים את אשר אני מוצא שנאכלת לשני ימים? הרי השווית את כולן! והיכן אני מוצא? כשהוא אומר: "אם נדר", הרי מצאתי שיש חגיגה נאכלת לשני ימים. ואיזו היא? על כרחיך, לימד על חגיגת י"ד כו'. והאיך לימד? דעל כרחיך, אי נמי "אם נדר" בחגיגת ט"ו משוית ליה — דקילא, דאינה באה עם הפסח — שמעת בה מיהא דנאכלת לשני ימים, ו"ביום הראשון לבקר" על כרחיך לאו אחגיגת ט"ו קאי, אלא א"אשר תזבח בערב", ולימד שתאכלנה כל יום הראשון עד בקר שני:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:4:1.english: It then says - [The] Tanna [of the baraita states]: "And how do I uphold [that there is] a Festival peace-offering that is eaten for two days besides this one?" That is to say: With which Festival peace-offering besides this one do I uphold that which I find, that it is eaten for two days? Surely you have equated all of them! And where do I find [it]? When it says: "If [it be] a vow," behold, I have found that there is a Festival peace-offering that is eaten for two days. And which one is it? Perforce, it taught regarding the Festival peace-offering of the fourteenth, etc. And how did it teach [this]? For perforce, even if you equate "if [it be] a vow" with the Festival peace-offering of the fifteenth — which is more lenient, since it does not come with the Paschal offering — you learn from it at least that it is eaten for two days, and "on the first day until the morning" perforce does not refer to the Festival peace-offering of the fifteenth, rather to "which you sacrifice in the evening," and [thus] it taught that you may eat it all of the first day until the second morning.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:5:1.english: This [refers] to the Festival peace-offering of the fifteenth - [That is, the verse,] "If [it is] a vow."

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:5:2.english: And that entire other [verse] - [Including the phrase] "on the first day," as I explained [above].

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:6:1.hebrew: וטעמא דכתיב כו' - השתא מפרש אתקפתיה, דאילו תנא לבשר לא בעי ראשית — אי לא כתיב ביום הראשון לבקר דמשמע תרי, הוה אמינא בקר — בקר ראשון, ואע"ג דבבשר קאי דקיל, וכל שכן בקר דכתיב גבי חלב חגי דלא בעי ראשית. והאי דסמכינהו קרא, מילתא אחריתי דרוש בה:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:6:1.english: And the reason is that it is written, etc. - Now [the Gemara] explains his objection, that had [Scripture] taught [it] regarding meat, it would not require "first" — [for] if "on the first day until the morning" were not written, which implies two [days], I would say "morning" [means] the first morning, even though it refers to meat, which is more lenient; and all the more so "morning" that is written regarding the fat of my Festival offering, which does not require "first." And [as for] the fact that Scripture juxtaposed them, expound another matter from it.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:7:1.hebrew: הפסח ששחטו בשבת שלא לשמו - וכסבור, כשם שמותר לשמו, כך מותר שלא לשמו:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:7:1.english: A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered on Shabbat not for its own sake - And [he] assumed [that] just as it is permitted [to slaughter it] for its own sake, so too it is permitted not for its own sake.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:8:1.english: Liable [to bring] a sin-offering - For he desecrated Shabbat unwittingly.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:8:2.hebrew: אם אינן ראויין - לפסח, כגון עגל או איל בן שתי שנים או נקבה, חייב עליו חטאת אם נעלמה ממנו שבת או כסבור שמותר לשחוט אחרים לשם פסח בשבת, דהאי לאו טועה בדבר מצוה הוא, דהכל יודעין שאין זה כשר לפסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:8:2.english: If they are not fit - for the Paschal offering, such as a calf, or a two-year-old ram, or a female, he is liable for it [to bring] a sin-offering if Shabbat escaped his notice or [if] he thought that it is permitted to slaughter other [offerings] for the sake of a Paschal offering on Shabbat; for this [person] is not one who errs in a matter of a mitzva, since everyone knows that this is not valid for a Paschal offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:8:3.hebrew: ואם ראויין הן - כגון שהוא שה בן שנה של שלמים ששחטו לשם פסח, דמתוך שטרוד ובהול לשחוט פסחו, טעה בזה ולא נזכר שהקדישו לדבר אחר:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:8:3.english: And if they are fit - For example, where it is a one-year-old lamb of a peace-offering that he slaughtered for the sake of a Paschal offering, for since he is preoccupied and rushed to slaughter his Paschal offering, he erred with this [animal] and did not remember that he had consecrated it for another matter.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:8:4.hebrew: ר' אליעזר מחייב חטאת - אע"פ שטעה בדבר מצוה:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:8:4.english: Rabbi Eliezer deems [him] liable [to bring] a sin-offering - Even though he erred in a matter of a mitzvah.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:8:5.hebrew: ור' יהושע פוטר - דקסבר טעה בדבר מצוה ועשה מצוה כל דהו, פטור מחיוב חטאת שבה. וזה עשה מצוה, שהקריב קרבן, וכל הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן כשירין, ואף הנשחטין לשם הפסח — ר' יהושע מכשיר להו בפרק תמיד נשחט (פסחים ד' סב:):
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:8:5.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua exempts [him] - For he holds [that if] one erred in [attempting to perform] a mitzva and performed some mitzva, he is exempt from the sin-offering liability [incurred] through it. And this [person] performed a mitzva, as he offered a sacrifice, and all sacrifices that were slaughtered not for their own sake are valid; and even those slaughtered for the sake of the Paschal offering, Rabbi Yehoshua deems them valid in the chapter [entitled] Tamid Nishchat (Pesachim 62b).

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:9:1.hebrew: מה אם פסח שמותר - לשוחטו בשבת לשמו, שינה את שמו — מודית לי דחייב חטאת, כדקתני לעיל:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:9:1.english: If [with regard to] a Paschal lamb, which is permitted - to be slaughtered on Shabbat for its own purpose, [if] one changed its purpose, you agree with me that he is liable [to bring] a sin-offering, as was taught above.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:9:2.english: That he changed [it] for something forbidden - That he slaughtered it for the sake of other offerings, which are forbidden to be slaughtered on Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 71b:9:3.hebrew: ששינן בדבר המותר - ששחטן לשם פסח, שמותר לשוחטו בשבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 71b:9:3.english: That he changed them for something permitted - For he slaughtered them for the sake of a Paschal offering, which is permitted to be slaughtered on Shabbat.

Tosafot on Pesachim 71b:1:1.hebrew: לימד על חגיגת י"ד שנאכלת לשני ימים ולילה אחד - תימה לר"י, דתניא בסוף פרק כל הפסולים (זבחים לו): "ובשר זבח תודת שלמיו" — למדנו תודה שנאכלת ליום ולילה, מנין לרבות שלמי נזיר ושלמי פסח? ת"ל: "שלמיו". ופי' בקונ' התם: שלמים הבאים מחמת פסח — היינו חגיגת י"ד. והשתא ההיא ברייתא כמאן? דלתנא דשמעתין נאכלת לשני ימים, ולבן תימא (לעיל פסחים ד' ע.) נמי דנאכלת ליום ולילה נפקא ליה מדהוקש לפסח, והתם נפקא ליה מדכתיב "זבח תודת שלמיו"! על כן נראה לר"י דשלמים הבאים מחמת פסח דקתני התם היינו מותר הפסח שקרב שלמים. והשתא אתי שפיר, דלקמן פרק האשה (פסחים ד' פט.) אמרינן דמותר הפסח נאכל ליום ולילה, ומנא לן אי לא מקרא דהתם? ובת"כ בפרשת צו את אהרן משמע בהדיא כפי' ר"י, דדריש התם האי קרא ד"בשר זבח תודת שלמיו" לשלמים הבאים מחמת פסח, ובתר הכי מייתי ההיא דשמעתין, ודריש מ"לא ילין מן הבשר אשר תזבח בערב וגו'": בחגיגה הבאה עם הפסח הכתוב מדבר, שתאכל לשני ימים ולילה אחד. אלמא משמע דההיא דלעיל איירי במותר הפסח שקרב שלמים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 71b:1:1.english: "[This] teaches regarding the Festival peace-offering of the fourteenth that it is eaten for two days and one night" - This is astonishing to Rabbi Yitzchak, for it was taught in a baraita at the end of chapter Kol HaPesulim (Zevachim 36a): "'And the flesh of the sacrifice of his thanksgiving peace-offerings' — we have learned [regarding] a thanksgiving-offering that it is eaten for [one] day and [one] night; from where [do we learn] to include the peace-offerings of a nazirite and the peace-offerings of Pesach? Scripture states: 'his peace-offerings.'" And [Rashi] explained in the Kunteres there: "peace-offerings that come on account of the Pesach [offering]" — this refers to the Festival peace-offering of the fourteenth. Now, according to whom is that baraita [in Zevachim]? For according to the Tanna of our sugya, it is eaten for two days [and one night]; and according to Ben Teima (above, Pesachim 70a) as well, that it is eaten for [one] day and [one] night is derived by him from [the fact] that it was compared to the Pesach [offering], whereas there [in Zevachim] it is derived from that which is written, "the sacrifice of his thanksgiving peace-offerings"! Therefore, it appears to Rabbi Yitzchak that "peace-offerings that come on account of the Pesach [offering]" which it teaches there refers to the remainder of the Pesach [offering] that is offered as a peace-offering. And now this works out well, for later in chapter HaIshah (Pesachim 89a) we say that the remainder of the Pesach [offering] is eaten for [one] day and [one] night — and from where would we [know this] if not from the verse [cited] there? And in Torat Kohanim, in Parashat Tzav et Aharon, it is explicitly implied in accordance with Rabbi Yitzchak's explanation, for it expounds there this verse of "the flesh of the sacrifice of his thanksgiving peace-offerings" as [referring to] peace-offerings that come on account of the Pesach [offering], and afterward it brings that [exposition] of our sugya, and expounds from "none of the flesh which you sacrifice in the evening... shall remain overnight, etc.": "Scripture speaks of the Festival peace-offering that comes with the Pesach [offering], that it shall be eaten for two days and one night." Thus, it is implied that that [earlier exposition] deals with the remainder of the Pesach [offering] that is offered as a peace-offering.

Tosafot on Pesachim 71b:5:1.hebrew: והאיך כוליה קרא לחגיגת י"ד - תימה לרשב"א: כיון דכולי' קרא בחגיגת י"ד איירי, ומאי "בקר"? בקר שני, א"כ תאכל לשני ימים ושני לילות! דקרא משמע שאינה נפסלת עד בקר שני, אבל ליל בקר שני נאכלת:
Tosafot on Pesachim 71b:5:1.english: And that other entire verse [refers] to the chagigah of the fourteenth - This is astonishing to Rashba: since the entire verse speaks of the chagigah of the fourteenth, and what is [meant by] "morning"? The second morning — if so, it should be eaten for two days and two nights! For the verse implies that it does not become disqualified until the second morning, so on the night of the second morning it may be eaten.

Tosafot on Pesachim 71b:6:1.hebrew: כל היכא דכתב בקר סתמא בקר ראשון - תימה לר"י, דבסוף ערבי פסחים (לקמן פסחים קכ:) דריש "בקר" — בקר שני, אף על גב דכתיב סתמא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 71b:6:1.english: Wherever "morning" is written unspecified, [it refers to] the first morning - This is perplexing to the Ri, for at the end of [the chapter] Arvei Pesachim (below, Pesachim 120b), [the Gemara] expounds "morning" [as] the second morning, even though it is written unspecified.
